question: Why does Xplain recommend premium publishers use attention-based KPIs instead of completion and viewability metrics?
transcript_excerpt: Fabien explains that completion and viewability metrics fail to capture the true quality premium publishers deliver. Attention-based KPIs that measure ad clutter, share of screen, time in view, sound rate, and quality of context create a multifactorial definition of quality. This allows premium publishers to objectively demonstrate their value to brands and differentiate from non-premium publishers, whereas traditional metrics treat all impressions equally.

question: What are the main flaws in post-click and post-view attribution models that advertisers commonly use?
transcript_excerpt: Post-click attribution favors users most likely to convert, incentivizing retargeting of users already about to purchase rather than acquiring new customers. Post-view attribution is even worse, encouraging sellers to ignore impression quality entirely and focus on cookie-bombing users with unseen or non-viewable impressions just to get credited for the last touch before a conversion, regardless of whether the impression actually drove value.

question: How should brands adapt their strategy for indexing and visibility in an LLM-driven search environment?
transcript_excerpt: Brands must win on two fronts: first, ensuring they are properly indexed and named in LLM responses so they exist among the options; second, building trust and familiarity so that when LLMs display multiple options, users select the brand they know best. This requires focusing on SEO to be indexed by LLMs while simultaneously building top-of-mind awareness through brand attention metrics, not just immediate conversion.

question: According to Jounce reports cited at their summit, what was the reduction in programmatic spend directed to MFA sites between recent years and 2026?
